title: Recipient priority matrix and fallback playbook
content:
Purpose and scope

This working doc captures UX notes, decision criteria, and initial wireframe ideas for a recipient-priority matrix and fallback playbook inside Redwood Console's Alerts & SLO surface. Goal: let tenants express who gets notified for which SLO class and what fallback paths should be used when primary channels fail or are muted. Primary audience: product/design + infra oncall + customer success.

Motivation / user problems
- Customers need predictable, auditable notification behavior when SLOs degrade (who gets paged, through what channel).
- Simple channel lists are insufficient for multi-tenant defaults + route-level overrides + temporary quiet windows.
- Failures happen: Slack outages, mobile push flakiness, email delays. We need explicit fallback semantics.
- Operators want low-noise escalation patterns (dedupe across channels, backoff timing, aggregate vs per-incident).

Core concepts (vocabulary)
- Recipient persona: a role-like grouping (oncall-engineer, infra-oncall, product-owner, exec-proxy) that maps to a contact method or a rotation.
- Channel: delivery mechanism (Slack channel, paging SMS, email, webhook, mobile push).
- Priority tier: severity bucket (P0/P1/P2) derived from SLO class + route properties.
- Fallback policy: ordered list of (recipient persona + channel) with timing/backoff and conditions.
- Quiet window / channel-suppression: tenant-level schedule to mute noisy channels while still allowing high-severity escalation.

Suggested UX surface (high-level)
1) Recipient matrix editor (card/grid)
   - Columns: Priority tier (P0-P2), Primary recipient persona, Primary channel, Fallback 1, Fallback 2, Escalation delay, Dedup window
   - Rows: default tenant row + per-route override rows (collapsible)
   - Inline editable chips for personas, channel dropdowns with small icons
   - A small preview (right-side) showing: "If SLO breach at 03:12, notifications: Slack #infra-oncall (0s) -> SMS oncall (60s) -> Email ops-lead (10m)"

2) Persona manager modal
   - Create persona -> map to rotation (PagerDuty/Oncall roster), static users, or external contacts
   - Allow tags (e.g., 'always-include', 'escalate-only')

3) Fallback playbook editor (per-priority)
   - Timeline visual: each lane shows action (notify) + channel + conditions (only if not-delivered / no-ack)
   - Action types: notify, wait-for-ack (with timeout), escalate, annotate-incident (add context), run-webhook
   - 'Simulate' button to step through 3 example failure modes (channel down, no ack, rate limit exceeded)

Wireframe notes (quick)
- Main grid: compact, single-line per row; expand to show full policy timeline
- Chips: persona (blue), channel (gray), delay badge (thin red text)
- Preview pane: human readable sentence + timeline graphic
- Empty state: "Add a priority mapping to get notified when an SLO begins to breach" plus CTA to persona manager

Edge behaviors and rules (proposal)
- Dedup across channels: default dedup window = 300s per incident; notifications within window are collapsed to one incident digest unless configured otherwise
- Channel health detection: system-level signals (500 errors from webhook, Slack API rate limit) flip channel into degraded state; when degraded, automatically skip to next fallback and flag the incident metadata
- Quiet windows: channel suppression only hides the channel; escalation can still occur after tier-appropriate delay to an always-on channel (SMS/pager) if configured
- Cross-tenant defaults: tenants can inherit org default matrix; explicit per-route or per-service overrides are highlighted in UI with pill: "overrides org default"
- Severity escalation amplification: if SLO moves from P2 -> P1 within X minutes, optionally expand recipients (auto-include product-owner)

Data model implications (rough)
- policy_id -> list of ordered targets: [{persona_id, channel_id, delay_seconds, condition_flags}] (we'll coordinate with backend but keep UX-first)
- persona object: {display_name, type: rotation|user|group, contacts: [ids], tags}
- channel object: {type, label, metadata: webhook/url/slack_channel}
- audit trail: each notification attempt recorded with outcome + fallback trigger id

Acceptance criteria for MVP
- Create/edit recipient personas (rotation + static) -> saved and available across tenant
- Default priority matrix row editable and applied to a test route
- Fallback timeline editor with 3 levels (primary + fallback1 + fallback2) and preview simulation
- Channel skipping when health flagged by backend (stubbed integration ok)

Backlog & grooming notes (estimated t-shirt sizes)
- Persona CRUD UI + roster integration (M) -- includes PD + Calendar sync
- Channel picker with health badges (S) -- read-only health status initially
- Priority matrix grid w/ expand timeline (L) -- inline editing + save/rollback
- Simulation runner (S) -- fake APi to step through outcomes
- Quiet window scheduler UI + tenant override (M)
- Dedup and incident-aggregation controls (M)
- Endpoint for audit trail + per-notification status (backend) (L)

Open questions / discussion items
- Should we allow per-alert-rule custom backoffs (e.g., exponential) or only fixed delays? Recommendation: MVP fixed delays; revisit after telemetry.
- How to present billing/usage impact for escalations that use SMS/paging (customers should be aware sms costs)? Suggest inline tooltip with estimated per-escalation cost.
- Multichannel acknowledgement semantics: if user ack via Slack, should we suppress SMS that is already enqueued? (Yes, but requires cross-channel ack signal). Need backend support.
- How to make persona shareable across tenants (for org-level teams) without leaking contacts? Probably persona templates (metadata only) + tenant-specific bindings.

Prototype notes / quick flows to capture in figma
- Flow A: tenant sets default matrix -> triggers test breach -> user views timeline simulation and confirms
- Flow B: route-level override created by SRE -> has 'temporary' checkbox (auto-expire in 24h)
- Flow C: channel degraded while notifying -> fallback is executed and there is a visible banner on incident: "Slack API unavailable, escalated to SMS"

Telemetry and observability hooks to add
- metric: fallback_triggered_count by channel_type
- metric: avg-time-to-first-ack by priority tier
- logs: per-notification outcome (success/failure/retry)
- alert: rapid fallback flood (indicates upstream channel outage)

Security & compliance considerations
- Contacts and rotation data are PII-like -> ensure RBAC for persona manager (only admins and oncall managers)
- Audit trail retention policy (90 days default, enterprise tier configurable)

Next steps (short-term)
- Align on data model with infra team (Arjun) — action: sync 09/03
- Quick figma mock of grid + persona modal (Maya) — deliver by EOW
- Wire up simulation harness prototype in staging for demo (Tomás)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally UX-forward; backend shape is provisional. Please focus on: clarity of mapping between persona/channel/priority; whether timeline/simulation covers realistic failure modes; and whether the grid layout is scannable for large tenant configs.

Attachments / references

- Link: JIRA-OPS-482 (backend schema spike)
